This release overhauls the in-process SDK MCP server. Twelve gaps against the
Python SDK were found by running the code rather than reading it, and all
twelve are closed — including one the CLI exercises on every timed-out tool
call.

## ⚠️ Breaking

**`McpSdkServerConfig.instance()` is now an `McpMessageHandler`.** It is a
`record`, so both the accessor's return type *and* the canonical constructor's
descriptor changed — code compiled against 0.1.24 that reads **or constructs**
one needs a recompile. If you build configs with `SdkMcpServer.toConfig()`, the
documented path, you are unaffected.

**An unknown tool is now an `isError` result, not JSON-RPC `-32601`**, with
Python's exact wording `Tool '<name>' not found`. An `isError` result reaches
the model, which can read it and correct itself; a JSON-RPC error never does.

**A tool whose `inputSchema` is not valid JSON Schema is no longer callable.**
Validation fails *closed*, as Python's does: each schema is checked against its
dialect's meta-schema when the server is built. This is not hypothetical
strictness — the validator accepted a malformed schema and then mis-validated
against it, so `{"type": "bogus"}` made every call fail citing the *caller's*
arguments, and `"properties": "a string"` waved every call through unchecked.
Vendor/unknown keywords remain legal.

## Highlights

**A running tool can now be cancelled.** When a tool outruns `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`
the CLI sends `notifications/cancelled` — previously answered with a `-32601`
(a response to a notification, which JSON-RPC forbids) while the tool kept
running with its side effects. The call is now settled with `-32800` and the
handler is signalled. Because `CompletableFuture.cancel(true)` does **not**
interrupt a running task, stopping real work needs an explicit signal:

```java
SdkMcpTool<Map<String, Object>> crawl = SdkMcpTool.create(
    "crawl", "Fetch every page under a URL", schema,
    (args, context) -> CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> {
        for (String url : urlsFrom(args)) {
            if (context.isCancelled()) {
                break;                    // nobody is waiting any more
            }
            pages.add(fetch(url));
        }
        return ToolResult.text(String.join("\n", pages));
    }));
```

Existing one-argument handlers compile and behave exactly as before.
`onCancel(Runnable)` covers work that cannot poll; `@Tool` methods may declare
a `ToolCallContext` parameter, which is injected and never published in the
schema.

**Bring your own MCP server.** `McpSdkServerConfig` now holds an
`McpMessageHandler`, so you can serve parts of MCP the built-in server does
not — resources, prompts, completions — or adapt a third-party MCP library,
without the SDK taking that dependency on everyone's behalf.

**Protocol version negotiation.** The client's requested version was ignored
and `2024-11-05` returned unconditionally. The server now advertises
`2025-06-18` and `2024-11-05` and negotiates properly. `2025-03-26` is
deliberately *not* claimed: it made JSON-RPC batching mandatory to receive, and
a batch is a top-level array, which the control request carrying these messages
types as a map and cannot represent.

**Richer tool results.** `ToolResult.json(...)` and `ToolResult.ofContent(...)`
were documented but did not exist; both are real now, alongside `addJson`,
`addResourceLink`, `addResource` and `addContent`, porting Python's content
conversion. `ping` is answered.

## Fixed

- A notification no longer receives a JSON-RPC response, which JSON-RPC forbids
- A message with no `method` no longer throws `NullPointerException` out of
  `handleMessage`; malformed `params` is `-32602`
- `"arguments": null` no longer reaches the handler as `null`
- A tool's `title` is no longer dropped when it declares no annotations
- An unknown server or a failing handler fails only that MCP call, not the whole
  control request
- The 60-second cap on an SDK MCP tool is gone — it bounded nothing (the tool
  kept running) while turning "slow" into "broken"
- Closing a client no longer waits out the control-executor join timeout
- An `Error` thrown while handling a control request no longer vanishes,
  leaving the CLI waiting forever

## On the official MCP Java SDK

`io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk` 2.0.1 was evaluated and deliberately not adopted.
It is published by Anthropic, targets Java 17, and its `mcp-json-jackson2`
module pins the very `json-schema-validator` this SDK already uses — but
`mcp-core` hard-depends on `reactor-core`, which would add roughly 2.5&nbsp;MB
(three quarters of it Reactor) to a ~3&nbsp;MB runtime footprint and sit oddly
beside this SDK's virtual-thread idiom. As of 2.0.1 it also has no
`notifications/cancelled` support of its own, so the headline gap would have
remained ours to fix regardless. The `McpMessageHandler` SPI is the answer
instead: anyone who wants the full protocol surface can adapt the official SDK
in their own project and pay for Reactor there.

## Also

Four examples were repaired — `ToolUsage` aborted halfway through on too tight
a turn budget, and `PermissionCallbacks` had three of its four sections
silently shadowed by settings-file allow rules, so the callbacks never fired.

50 new tests (1032 total), including the first end-to-end coverage of an
`mcp_message` control request — the gap that let four of these defects survive.
